title: Unify lightweight trace bridge and decouple metric emitters for lower tail-latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor the tracing and metrics pipeline to introduce a zero-copy trace bridge, consolidate trace hook integration points across services, and decouple metric emission from request hot paths. Goal is to reduce p95/p99 tail latency caused by synchronous trace/metric serialization and reduce memory allocations during high-concurrency workloads.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end traces preserved with existing span metadata and resource attributes after bridge enablement
Background metric emissary handles non-critical emitters; no synchronous blocking on request path for >99% of requests
Observed reduction in median allocations per request by >=30% in bench harness and p99 tail latency improvement of at least 10% for runtime RPCs
Compatibility tests pass against current vendor exporters and our internal observability-forwarder (integration test suite)
Feature gated rollout: toggle can be enabled per-service and with gradual traffic ramp-up in console
technical_notes: Introduce a thin 'trace bridge' process/worker that accepts raw span write buffers via a lock-free ring buffer; worker performs final encoding and forwarding to exporter asynchronously
Replace current inline OTEL exporter calls in high-traffic codepaths with ring-buffer enqueue operations to avoid allocations and syscall spins

Decouple sample-rate and metric emission logic: non-critical metrics (cache hits, batching stats) are aggregated in-memory and flushed on timer or backpressure, critical metrics remain immediate but are minimized
Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK to v1.15.0 to leverage batched span processors and improved context propagation helpers; validate API changes for our language runtimes
Add golden serialization tests and backward-compat encoding checks to ensure downstream exporters accept bridged payloads
Keep a compatibility shim for services that cannot adopt the bridge immediately; shim will forward to existing exporters unchanged
